## Manchester Boiler Breakdown Checklist

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/thermometer-half.svg

A broken boiler in a rented flat should be treated as a priority because there is no hot water and a young child is in the home. Keep everything calm, factual, and time-stamped from the first report onward.

## What to Keep and What to Send

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/clipboard-check.svg

- **Incident log:** note the boiler stopped working on **2026-01-18**, when you noticed it, and every follow-up message.
- **Proof of notice:** save the message sent to the landlord on the same day, plus any replies.
- **Photos/video:** take clear photos of the boiler display, error codes, leaks, or any thermostat issues.
- **Impact notes:** record that there is **no hot water**, the flat is **2 bedrooms**, and a **3-year-old child** is affected.
- **Repair trail:** keep appointment times, missed visits, engineer names, and any promised dates.
- **Costs:** keep receipts if you need temporary alternatives, such as laundrette costs, extra heating, or bottled water.
- **Communication copies:** store texts, emails, call logs, and voicemail screenshots in one folder.

## Practical Tenant Action Checklist

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar2-week.svg

- **Today:** send a short written follow-up asking for the repair date and whether an engineer has been booked.
- **Next message:** mention the child’s age and that the flat has no hot water, so you need a prompt update.
- **If the landlord gives a date:** confirm it back in writing so there is one clear record.
- **If no response after a reasonable delay:** send a polite reminder asking for an update and a realistic repair timeline.
- **If the repair is delayed again:** ask whether a temporary solution is available, such as a replacement boiler part, portable heater, or interim hot water arrangement.
- **If the issue continues:** keep escalating in writing, step by step, without arguing by phone alone.
- **Keep the home safe:** if you use any temporary heating, follow basic safety guidance and keep it away from a child’s reach.

## Polite Escalation Message Flow


- **Message 1:** report the fault clearly and ask for an urgent repair time.
- **Message 2:** follow up politely if there is no reply or no booked visit.
- **Message 3:** request a firm update and ask who is handling the repair.
- **Message 4:** if still delayed, say the issue is ongoing and affecting day-to-day living, especially because there is no hot water for a household with a young child.
- **Message 5:** ask for written confirmation of the expected repair date and any temporary arrangements.

## Suggested Message Template

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/envelope-paper.svg

Hello [Landlord/Agent Name],

I’m following up on the boiler fault reported on **2026-01-18**. The boiler is still not working, we have **no hot water**, and this is affecting our **2-bedroom flat** and our **3-year-old child**.

Please let me know:
- when the repair has been booked
- the expected engineer visit date
- whether any temporary solution is available in the meantime

Thank you for your help. I’d appreciate a written update when possible.

Kind regards,
[Your Name]

## Sources

- Manchester City Council housing guidance: https://www.manchester.gov.uk/info/100003/housing
- UK Government rented housing guidance: https://www.gov.uk/private-renting
- Citizens Advice repairs in rented housing: https://www.citizensadvice.org.uk/housing/renting-privately/repairs-in-private-rented-housing/
